paragraphs: May's Diary, Saturday night. Dear diary, Today the Explorers walked along the old town trail with Teacher Kim. The trail is two kilometers long. It was a cloudy morning, but it was warm. Lily walked next to me, and she took notes for the blog. At the beginning, we stood at an old wooden gate. Our guide was a woman with a green bag and a loud voice. She said, "Stay together, and listen to me."

We walked slowly along the narrow street. First, we passed a market with fruit and flowers. A woman at the market gave us a small slice of mango. It was sweet and cold. Next, we passed a small bridge over a canal. Many tourists took photos of the old houses. I heard people who spoke other languages. I asked myself, "Why do tourists like old towns?" Leo said, "Because the houses tell stories." I think that he is right.

At eleven o'clock, it began to rain. The guide looked at the sky and looked at the group. "We will decide now," said Teacher Kim. "Shall we walk in the rain or go indoors?" Everybody wanted to go indoors, so we ran to a small museum. It was in an old house with a wooden floor. We were wet, but the room was warm and dry. The house is one hundred years old, and the clock still works.

Inside, there were old photos, old maps, and a big clock. The guide gave us a quiz about the photos. "Which photo shows the market?" she asked. I knew the answer, and I pointed at the photo. Leo answered three questions, and I answered four. Lily answered five questions. There was no winner, because the quiz was for fun. At the end, every child got a small prize. It was a postcard of the old town.
I will put my postcard on my wall tomorrow. I am happy about today, because it was an interesting walk. Even the rain was fun. Which old place do you like in your town? Good night, diary.
